**Finding: Compliant (preferred position) — no redline proposed.**

The agreement imposes no minimum purchase commitment on the Company:

- **Section 3.1** is a pure usage-based revenue share — 30% of actual Net Sales, and only on Net Sales *above* an $11,000/month threshold. That threshold benefits us (it shields the first $11,000 of monthly sales from any fee); it is not a floor we must pay up to.
- **No shortfall, make-whole, take-or-pay or volume-cap language** appears anywhere — targeted searches for "minimum", "commit", and "guarantee" returned no hits.
- **Section 4.1** gives a one-year term with annual auto-renewal, terminable by either Party on 90 days' notice, so there is no multi-year lock-in even at the fallback level.

Two adjacent items noted in the rationale but deliberately not flagged here:
- **Section 4.2 Termination Payment** — an exit-fee formula (12-month Net Sales less $800,000, halved, floored at zero). This is an exit charge, not a purchase commitment, and is properly assessed under the termination/exit-fee rule rather than double-counted under MINCOMMIT.
- **Section 6.1 Exclusivity** — a channel restriction on the Company, not a volume cap on usage; it belongs to the exclusivity rule.
